raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On HIP, `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` fuses the shared expert into the AITER MoE only at TP4 and TP8 (#41161; Quark MXFP4 added in #41870, measured at TP4). At TP2 the shared expert runs as separate MXFP4 GEMMs and is added to the routed output.

This PR admits TP2 for Quark MXFP4 checkpoints. The fused path does not depend on the TP size without expert parallelism:
- The shared expert is loaded into slot 288 and TP-sharded like the routed experts (1024 per rank at TP2).
- The router appends that slot with weight 1.0 for every token.

Scope:
- Models: `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` with Quark MXFP4 experts (e.g. `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`). Measured: that model at TP2. The NextN draft has its own gate and is not changed.
- Platform: ROCm, AITER on gfx950, TP2 with EP1 and no MoE all-to-all backend, as for TP4/TP8.
- Unchanged: block FP8 (still TP4/TP8), TP1/TP16, CUDA.

Fusion is on by default whenever the gate admits it, so TP2 Quark MXFP4 servers now fuse unless `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` is passed.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py`: in `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`, the HIP TP check accepts TP2, TP4 and TP8 when the quant config is Quark, and TP4 and TP8 otherwise; the refusal message names the TP set that applies. The Quark MXFP4 layout check that follows is unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` (CPU): the Quark MXFP4 admission case runs at TP2, TP4 and TP8 (TP2 fails without this change), and a Quark config at TP1 is still refused.

AITER at the pinned commit (`285579b6`) has no tuned MXFP4 fused-MoE rows for GLM-5.3-Flash at TP2, either for the routed-only shape (E=288, top-k 8, inter_dim 1024) or the fused one (E=289, top-k 9). Both run AITER's default configs. This is also the case for MXFP4 at TP4/TP8 today. ROCm/aiter#6435 (merged after the pin) adds tuned rows for both shapes.

## Accuracy Tests

Fusion changes the numerics: the shared expert's activation quantization and its accumulation into the MoE output differ from the separate path, so outputs are not bitwise identical.

- GSM8K (`sgl-eval run gsm8k`, sgl-eval 0.1.3, all 1319 problems, `--num-threads 32 --max-tokens 32768`, temperature 0; server as below with `--context-length 40960`; one launch per arm): baseline 97.19 % (1282), this PR 97.27 % (1283), +0.08 pp; paired by problem, 10 correct only in the baseline and 11 only in this PR. Thinking was on in both arms (about 195 reasoning tokens per answer), so these are not comparable to the non-thinking numbers in the model docs.
- Mean probability of the gold answer letter (P(gold)) over 805 single-image multiple-choice MMMU validation items, thinking off, concurrency 1, two launches per arm, paired by item: baseline 0.6539, this PR 0.6533, drop +0.06 pp (95 % CI −0.67 … +0.79 pp).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup**

- Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261024` with its default environment; SGLang imported through `PYTHONPATH` from the `python/` tree of the base `bf1a2529` (baseline) or of this PR. AITER `285579b6` (the pin), ROCm 7.2.4.
- 2x MI355X (gfx950), TP2, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` at revision `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`.
- Server, identical in both arms (no `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, so the gate decides):
  ```bash
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
    --revision b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07 --quantization quark --tp-size 2 \
    --attention-backend dsa --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
    --linear-attn-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --moe-runner-backend aiter \
    --disable-radix-cache --context-length 8192 \
    --max-running-requests 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.92 --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":true,"num_threads":8}' \
    --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-multimodal \
    --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image": 1}' \
    --mm-process-config '{"image": {"min_image_tokens": 16, "max_image_tokens": 8000}}' \
    --mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0 --mm-enable-dp-encoder --mm-attention-backend aiter_attn
  ```
- Benchmark, per concurrency 4, 16, 32 and 64, two measured runs each after one warm-up pass:
  ```bash
  python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name image \
    --image-resolution 512x512 --image-count 1 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.8 --request-rate inf --seed 42 --max-concurrency "$c" --num-prompts $((10 * c))
  ```
- Launch order: baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline.

**Results** (means over 2 launches × 2 runs per arm; mean TTFT and TPOT):

| Concurrency | Output tok/s | TTFT (ms) | TPOT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 300.4 → 332.7 (+10.8 %) | 199.3 → 177.1 (−11.2 %) | 11.54 → 10.44 (−9.5 %) |
| 16 | 610.3 → 664.4 (+8.9 %) | 327.3 → 307.4 (−6.1 %) | 23.08 → 21.16 (−8.3 %) |
| 32 | 806.2 → 852.4 (+5.7 %) | 464.4 → 435.7 (−6.2 %) | 35.42 → 33.52 (−5.4 %) |
| 64 | 977.3 → 1037.4 (+6.2 %) | 655.5 → 634.6 (−3.2 %) | 59.51 → 55.90 (−6.1 %) |

- Mean output tok/s change over c16-c64: +6.9 %, standard error 0.51 % (from the run-to-run spread of repeated baseline-vs-baseline launches on this setup).
- KV cache: 15,506,944 → 15,488,256 tokens (−0.12 %).
- Activation: every launch of this PR logs `Shared experts fusion optimization enabled.` and only AITER fused-MoE selections with E=289, top-k 9; every baseline launch logs `HIP shared experts fusion is validated only for TP4 and TP8. Shared experts fusion optimization is disabled.` and only E=288, top-k 8.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
  - `test/registered/unit/models/test_shared_experts_fusion_gates.py` (CPU): 49 passed. Without the `glm5_next.py` change, `test_quark_mxfp4_is_admitted_at_tp2_tp4_and_tp8` fails at `tp_size=2`.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No option or API change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Notes

- #42268 admits TP2 for block FP8 and keeps Quark MXFP4 at TP4/TP8 with an explicit TP2 refusal. This PR admits that Quark MXFP4 case, with end-to-end measurements, and leaves block FP8 at TP4/TP8. The two conflict on the Quark TP2 refusal: if #42268 lands first, this PR reduces to removing it; if this PR lands first, #42268 can drop it and use one TP set for both quant types.
- The same change for vLLM: vllm-project/vllm#63603.
- This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed.
